People in B.C. are headed to the polls in October for municipal elections across the province.

At the same time, local newsrooms have been gutted, with existing reporting teams trying to do more with less.

Local politics are hugely consequential for how we live day to day but often have the lowest voter turnouts of any kinds of elections.

The Tyee’s independent journalists are on the ground, tracking candidates and issues across the province.

And we’re asking our readers what is most important to you this civic election season.

That’s because we work for you. Our non-profit newsroom is funded in large part directly by our readers, who we call Tyee Builders. As a Builder, you can contribute an amount that works for you, on your schedule, and help support the public interest journalism that is crucial during the democratic process. Stated Claim / Post Context:
A Utah licensing board wants to ban a former therapist for at least 5 years. His supporters rallied to his defense.

Maurice Harker pleaded no contest to charges involving a former patient. As supporters defended him, the former patient told a licensing board: “I’m not lying.”

Actual Article Body:
(Rick Egan | The Salt Lake Tribune) Maurice Harker attends a hearing at the Behavioral Health Board meeting at the Division of Professional Licensing on Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026.

Comment

Add as Preferred Source

To Maurice Harker’s supporters, a licensing board’s recommendation Thursday to stop him from returning to work as a therapist threatened to deprive others of help.

To the former patient who reported that he restrained and injured her during sessions, it was the right step.

The Behavioral Health Board recommended that Harker be barred from applying for a therapy license for five years, after the former-therapist-turned-life-coach pleaded no contest to charges in connection to the patient’s report.
